lessons.title: Time and work, pipes and cisterns (made easy)
lessons.summary: One simple idea solves every work question: imagine the job as a number of small pieces, count how many pieces each person does in a day, and add them up.

sections.html:
Two painters

A painter can paint a wall in 4 hours. His helper takes 6 hours. Working together, how long? Many people say 5 hours. That can't be right: with a helper, the job must finish sooner than 4 hours.

Here is the trick. Pretend the wall has 12 tiles. We pick 12 because both 4 and 6 divide into it exactly.

WhoTime aloneTiles per hour
Painter4 hours12 ÷ 4 = 3
Helper6 hours12 ÷ 6 = 2
Together?3 + 2 = 5

Together they paint 5 tiles an hour, so 12 tiles take 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4 hours (2 hours 24 minutes). That is the whole topic: pick a job size, find each person's pieces per day, add them, divide.

A takes 10 days and B takes 15 days. Pretend the job is 30 pieces. How many pieces does A do in a day?

  1. 2
  2. 3
  3. 5
Watch the 12-tile wall get painted
Each hour 3 gold + 2 green = 5 tiles. Two full hours do 10; the last 2 tiles need 2/5 of an hour.

1. Pick the job size: a number that every given time divides into exactly. (This is the LCM; for 10 and 15, 30 works.)
  2. Pieces per day for each person = job size ÷ their days.
  3. Add the pieces per day of everyone working together.
  4. Days needed = job size ÷ total pieces per day.

Then check: the answer must be less than the fastest person's time alone.

How to pick the job size quickly

Take the biggest number and go up its times table until the others divide it. For 12 and 18: 18 ✗, 36 ✓. So 36.

A can finish a job in 12 days, B in 18 days. How long together?

StepWorking
Job size36 (12 and 18 both divide 36)
A per day36 ÷ 12 = 3
B per day36 ÷ 18 = 2
Together per day3 + 2 = 5
Days36 ÷ 5 = 7.2 days

Check: 7.2 is less than 12 ✓

Shortcut for exactly two people

Multiply the two times and divide by their sum: (12 × 18) ÷ (12 + 18) = 216 ÷ 30 = 7.2 days. Use it once the tile method feels easy.

A takes 20 days and B takes 30 days. Together they take:

  1. 12 days
  2. 25 days
  3. 10 days
A (12 days) and B (18 days) on a 36-piece job
36 ÷ 12 = 3 a day for A, 36 ÷ 18 = 2 a day for B. Seven full days do 35 pieces; the last piece takes 1/5 of a day.

Sometimes you are told the time together and must find one person's time. Same table, but subtract. A and B together take 8 days. A alone takes 12 days. How long does B take alone?

  • Job size: 24 (8 and 12 both divide 24).
  • Together per day: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. A per day: 24 ÷ 12 = 2.
  • So B does 3 − 2 = 1 piece a day, and 24 ÷ 1 = 24 days.

A and B together take 10 days. A alone takes 15 days. B alone takes:

  1. 25 days
  2. 30 days
  3. 5 days

There are two kinds of question. Read carefully which one it is. Type 1: "A leaves after 6 days." Start from the beginning. A takes 20 days, B takes 30. Job = 60, so A does 3 a day and B 2 a day.

  • First 6 days together: 6 × 5 = 30 pieces done.
  • 30 pieces left for B alone at 2 a day: 15 more days.
  • Total: 6 + 15 = 21 days.

Type 2: "A leaves 5 days before the end." Start from the end. A takes 10 days, B takes 15. Job = 30, so A does 3 a day and B 2 a day.

  • In the last 5 days only B works: 5 × 2 = 10 pieces.
  • The other 20 pieces were done together at 5 a day: 4 days.
  • Total: 4 + 5 = 9 days.
Spot the type

"After x days" means start from the beginning. "x days before the end" or "before completion" means start from the end.

A takes 20 days and B takes 30 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. B finishes the rest in:

  1. 20 days
  2. 22 days
  3. 16 days
A leaves after 6 days (A 20 days, B 30 days, job 60)
First 6 days: 5 a day = 30. The other 30 pieces at 2 a day take B 15 more days. Total 21.

sections.h: Pipes and leaks: the same thing
sections.html:
A pipe filling a tank is just a worker. A pipe that empties the tank, or a leak, is a worker who undoes work, so you subtract it. Pipe A fills a tank in 4 hours. Pipe B empties it in 6 hours. With both open, how long to fill it?

  • Tank = 12 pieces. A adds 3 an hour; B removes 2 an hour.
  • Net: 3 − 2 = 1 an hour, so 12 hours.

With an emptying pipe the answer can be longer than the filling pipe alone. That is correct. A leak question. A pipe fills a tank in 5 hours, but with a leak it takes 6 hours. How long would the leak take to empty a full tank?

  • Tank = 30. The pipe alone adds 6 an hour. With the leak, the tank gains 30 ÷ 6 = 5 an hour.
  • So the leak removes 6 − 5 = 1 an hour: 30 hours.

Pipes A and B fill a tank in 10 h and 15 h; pipe C empties it in 12 h. With all three open, the empty tank fills in:

  1. 8 h
  2. 12 h
  3. 20 h
Pipe A fills in 4 h, pipe B empties in 6 h (tank = 12)

"A is twice as fast as B" means A does 2 pieces while B does 1, so A takes half of B's time. If B takes 30 days, A takes 15. "A is 50% more efficient than B" means A does 150 while B does 100, a ratio of 3 : 2. Times go the other way: 2 : 3. If B takes 30 days, A takes 20 days (not 15). Wages are shared by how much work each person did. A takes 10 days and B 15 days. They do the job together and are paid ₹5,000. Job 30: A does 3 a day, B 2 a day, so they share 3 : 2. A gets 3/5 of ₹5,000 = ₹3,000.

A is three times as fast as B and takes 20 days less to finish a job. A alone takes:

  1. 10 days
  2. 15 days
  3. 30 days

Think of the job as man-days: number of people × number of days. The same job always needs the same man-days. 8 men finish a job in 15 days. How many days will 10 men take?

  • Job = 8 × 15 = 120 man-days.
  • With 10 men: 120 ÷ 10 = 12 days.

If hours per day are given, count man-hours (men × days × hours). If the job is bigger, find the effort for one unit first. 12 men working 8 hours a day build a 48 m wall in 10 days. How many men, working 6 hours a day, are needed to build a 72 m wall in 16 days?

  • Effort for 48 m: 12 × 10 × 8 = 960 man-hours. So 1 m needs 960 ÷ 48 = 20 man-hours.
  • 72 m needs 72 × 20 = 1,440 man-hours.
  • Each man gives 16 × 6 = 96 hours, so 1,440 ÷ 96 = 15 men.

6 men finish a job in 20 days. How many days will 8 men take?

  1. 12 days
  2. 26 days
  3. 15 days

• Never add or average the times. Add the pieces per day.
  • People working together always finish sooner than the fastest one alone (unless something empties the tank).
  • Emptying pipe or leak: subtract.
  • "Leaves after x days": start at the beginning. "x days before the end": start at the end.
  • Wages: shared by work done.
  • Same job, same man-days (or man-hours).
Three pairs

"A + B take 12 days, B + C 15, C + A 20." Job 60: the pair rates are 5, 4 and 3, which add to 12. That counts everyone twice, so A + B + C do 6 a day and take 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days.

facts: Job size = a number all the times divide (LCM); pieces per day = job ÷ own time
Two people together (a and b days)
B alone, given A alone and A + B together
A is 50% more efficient than B
Wages are shared in the ratio of…
Same job = same man-days (men × days); with hours, man-hours
Leaves x days before the end
Peel off the last x days first
Add the pair rates and halve
traps: Times never add or average; only rates add.
Efficiency and time are in inverse ratio: 3 : 2 efficiency means 2 : 3 time.
Wages go by work done, so the faster worker gets the larger share.
A leak or outlet pipe is subtracted from the filling rate.
recap: Pretend the job is a number of pieces that every time divides into (the LCM).
Rate = units ÷ own time; time = work left ÷ combined rate.
Someone leaving: split the job into the joint part and the solo part.
Men and days: the same job always needs the same man-days (or man-hours).
Pipes are the same problem; outlets and leaks are negative work.

mcqs.q: A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. Working together, they finish it in:
mcqs.e: LCM 60 units. A = 3/day, B = 2/day, together 5/day; 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days.

mcqs.q: A and B together finish a job in 10 days. A alone takes 15 days. B alone takes:
mcqs.e: LCM 30 units. Together 3/day, A 2/day, so B = 1/day; 30 ÷ 1 = 30 days.

mcqs.q: 8 men can finish a job in 15 days. How many days will 10 men take?
One pipe fills a tank in 4 hours and another empties it in 6 hours. With both open, the empty tank fills in:
mcqs.e: LCM 12 units. Fill +3/h, empty −2/h, net 1/h; 12 ÷ 1 = 12 h.

mcqs.q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: When two people work the same days, wages are shared in the ratio of the days each takes alone
If A takes 10 days and B 15 days, together they take 6 days
If A is twice as efficient as B, A takes half of B's time
A leak in a tank is counted as negative work
mcqs.e: Wages go by work done. Working the same days, shares are in the ratio of rates, which is the inverse of the days each takes alone. The other three statements are correct.

mcqs.q: A, B and C can do a job alone in 12, 15 and 20 days. Working together they finish it in:
A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. B finishes the remaining work in:
mcqs.e: LCM 60. Together 5/day for 4 days = 20 units. Left 40 units; B at 2/day takes 20 days.

mcqs.q: A can do a job in 15 days and B in 10 days. They start together, but A leaves 5 days before the work is completed. The whole work takes:
mcqs.e: LCM 30. A = 2/day, B = 3/day. Last 5 days only B: 15 units. Remaining 15 units together at 5/day = 3 days. Total 3 + 5 = 8 days.

mcqs.q: A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They do it together and are paid ₹5,000. A's share is:
mcqs.e: LCM 30: rates 3 : 2. Same days worked, so A gets 3/5 of ₹5,000 = ₹3,000.

mcqs.q: 12 men working 8 hours a day build a 48 m wall in 10 days. How many men working 6 hours a day are needed to build a 72 m wall in 16 days?
mcqs.e: Effort for 48 m = 12 × 10 × 8 = 960 man-hours, so 20 man-hours per metre. 72 m needs 1,440 man-hours; each man gives 16 × 6 = 96 hours; 1,440 ÷ 96 = 15 men.

mcqs.q: A pipe can fill a tank in 5 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it takes 6 hours to fill the tank. The leak alone can empty the full tank in:
mcqs.e: LCM 30 units. Pipe 6/h, net 5/h, so the leak removes 1/h; 30 ÷ 1 = 30 h.

mcqs.q: [Tough] A and B can do a job in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. A, B and C together can do it in:
mcqs.e: LCM 60. Pair rates 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 = 2 × (A + B + C), so A + B + C = 6 units/day; 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days.

mcqs.q: [Tough] A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. Which of the statements is/are correct? 1. Working together they finish it in 12 days. 2. If they are paid ₹1,500 for the joint job, A's share is ₹600.
mcqs.e: LCM 60: A = 3/day, B = 2/day, together 5/day → 12 days, so 1 is correct. Shares are 3 : 2, so A gets 3/5 of ₹1,500 = ₹900, not ₹600; 2 is wrong (₹600 is B's share).

mcqs.q: [Tough] Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes. Both are opened together. After how many minutes should A be closed so that the tank is full in exactly 18 minutes?
mcqs.e: LCM 60 units. A = 3/min, B = 2/min. B runs all 18 minutes: 36 units. A must supply 60 − 36 = 24 units, which takes 24 ÷ 3 = 8 minutes.

mcqs.q: [Tough] A is 25% more efficient than B. B alone can do a job in 25 days. Working together, A and B finish it in:
mcqs.e: Efficiency A : B = 5 : 4, so time A : B = 4 : 5 and A takes 20 days. Together = 20 × 25/(20 + 25) = 500/45 = 100/9 = 11 1/9 days.
